$comment: ignoreCommand: skip the build when a commit changes NOTHING that ships.
Added 2026-09-06, after Vercel emailed that the free team had used 100% of its 10 GB
Deployment Storage. The cause was not traffic: 20 production deployments in about three
hours, and a large share of them docs-only commits that change no shipped byte and still
store a full build. Measured over the last 24 hours of history: 40 of 115 commits (35%)
EXIT CODES ARE THE OPPOSITE OF INTUITION: 0 SKIPS the build, non-zero BUILDS.
`git diff --quiet A B -- <paths>` exits 0 when there is NO difference, so diffing with the
documentation paths EXCLUDED lands on exactly the right answer: nothing left once docs are
IT FAILS OPEN, ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF AN ENTITLEMENT GATE. On a shallow
clone HEAD^ may not exist; git then exits 128, which is non-zero, which BUILDS. The
expensive mistake here is skipping a real build silently - it looks exactly like 'no
changes needed' - so every uncertain case must build.
PROVEN BOTH WAYS against real commits before it was trusted: docs(cost) and docs(handoff)
exit 0 (skip); the [billing] and [transactions] source commits exit 1 (build); a bad ref
exits 128 (build). A skip rule that has only been proven to skip is not proven.
